- `parseDuration(str)` accepts one or more `<integer><unit>` groups, units `d`, `h`, `m`, `s`, each unit at most once and in that order (largest first). Anything else — empty input, stray characters, a repeated unit, units out of order — throws `RangeError`.
- `formatDuration(ms)` returns the canonical form; zero is `0s`.
- Do not edit `duration.test.js`.

All 9 tests pass (`# pass 9 # fail 0`).

**Changes in `/root/verify/pr12688/realmodel/runs/head-2/ws/duration.js`:**

1. **Validation** — replaced the scanning `/(\d+)([dhms])/g` loop (which silently ignored anything it couldn't match) with an anchored pattern that encodes the grammar directly:
   ```js
   const DURATION_RE = /^(?:(\d+)d)?(?:(\d+)h)?(?:(\d+)m)?(?:(\d+)s)?$/;
   ```
   Each unit appears at most once, in largest-first position, so repeated units (`1h2h`), out-of-order units (`30m1h`), and stray characters (`1hxx30m`) simply fail to match. Non-string input is rejected before `exec`, and a match where every capture group is absent (only possible for `''`) throws. All failures raise `RangeError`.

2. **`formatDuration`** — returns `'0s'` when no parts are produced, instead of the empty string. `UNITS` is now an ordered array of `[unit, size]` pairs so both functions share one ordering source.

**Beyond the test file**, I checked the contract holds on cases the tests don't cover: `'1h 30m'`, `' 1h'`, `'1H'`, `'1h3'`, `'h30m'`, `'1s2d'`, `'+1h'`, `'1h-30m'`, non-ASCII digits, `'1h\n'` (JS `$` matches only at true end of input — rejected), and `NaN`/`null`/`5` all throw `RangeError`; `'0s'` → `0`, `'0h30m'` → `1800000`, `formatDuration(999)` → `'0s'`, `formatDuration(90061000)` → `'1d1h1m1s'`-style canonical output.

`duration.test.js` was not modified, and no other files exist in the repo to lint or build.
